# Aubergine

> A local, browser-based canvas of terminal sessions for running several coding agents at once. It shows which agent is waiting for you, queues and schedules tasks, gives each agent its own working copy of a repository, and groups work in projects; sessions keep running when the browser closes. Everything runs on your own computer (127.0.0.1 only). Free and open source (MIT). Needs macOS, tmux 3.2+, Node.js 22+. Install: npm install -g @meatgarden/aubergine.

## Start here

- [Landing page](https://thirstyeggplant.com/): what it does, install, FAQ
- [README](https://github.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/blob/main/README.md): full reference
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@meatgarden/aubergine): `npm install -g @meatgarden/aubergine`
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/main/install.sh): one-line installer that builds from the source (also needs pnpm), changes only ~/.aubergine and one link

- [Guide for agents](https://github.com/thirstyeggplant/aubergine/blob/main/docs/for-agents.md)

## Planned, not built yet

- Teams and connections: Multiplayer; Chat interface; Tickets and pull requests; Watches, webhooks and triage; Shared skills and a marketplace; Memory for people and rooms; Admin controls for models, sharing and strictness; A self-hosted team server; Sign-in for teams (SSO and MFA); Usage limits per person, token or agent; Read-only reports to share without sharing terminals; A phone view of the “For you” list; Reviewed connectors to company tools; More chat apps; Small internal web apps published to chosen people.
- Cloud: Sandboxed agents in the cloud; A pool of agents; Ready-made environments; Long, multi-phase work; One-command cloud deploy; Work you can see; MCP over HTTP, for agents on other machines; Tested Linux support; Shell integration beyond zsh.
- Control: Approval modes; Command policy and screening; Risk levels per repository; A full audit trail; Undo an agent's work; Admin controls; Model choice per terminal, task or schedule.
- Quality: Quality gates; Pull request review; Browser-driven testing; Plan before build; Task recipes; Outcome metrics; Incident write-ups: an agent investigates and drafts a postmortem.
- Everywhere: Published SDK; Editor extension; Desktop app; Windows support.

None of this exists today. Everything runs on one computer.
